evidence.description: Spec 082 FR-001 + open-routes table; the enforcement matrix is exercised by backend/tests/test_api_token_auth.py (route families x {no header, wrong token, empty bearer, install token}) and by tools/auth-proof/check_auth.py against a live instance.

falsification_tests: Any protected route (route families enumerated from the built app: projects, spec-studies, studies, terminal, settings, shutdown, indus-evidence, jobs) answering anything other than 401 without a token or with a wrong token, or answering 401 to the install token.
claims.text: Every backend route outside the spec's open list (GET /api/v1/health, the built frontend bundle at /, /static/signs) rejects a missing or incorrect token with HTTP 401 for all methods and accepts the install token, with enforcement in middleware so any future route is protected by default.

evidence.description: Spec 082 FR-002; backend/glossa_lab/auth.py uses secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and an atomic 0600 write; test_api_token_auth.py scans response bodies and captured logs for the token and asserts file permissions and token entropy properties.

falsification_tests: The token string found in any tracked file, any log line emitted during the test matrix, or any API response body; the token file existing with permissions broader than 0600 on POSIX; two generated tokens colliding or shorter than 43 characters.
claims.text: The install token is generated with a CSPRNG at no less than 256 bits, is stored only in the install data directory's api_token file (POSIX mode 0600) or in a process environment the operator set, and never appears in git, in any log, or in any API response.

evidence.description: Spec 082 FR-003 + FR-005; backend/tests/test_tray_token_auth.py covers the tray's token resolution and header use headlessly, the healthcheck's authenticated identity legs are covered in test_api_token_auth.py, and the proof kit exercises the live consumer paths end-to-end.

falsification_tests: Any named consumer failing against an authed test instance: the tray's shutdown falling back to the kill path because of a 401, the healthcheck failing its identity check while the token file is present and resolvable, an MCP tool call rejected for a missing header the server should have sent.
claims.text: With the token in place, every named first-party consumer keeps working: the tray (health poll, shutdown, Open Glossa Lab handoff, Copy API Token), the supervision healthcheck's identity verification, the desktop verify path built on it, the in-repo MCP server, and the MCP skill client.

evidence.description: Plan rotation procedure; test_api_token_auth.py rotates against a live TestClient app and asserts old-token 401, new-token success, data-dir byte-stability outside api_token, and value-free CLI output.

falsification_tests: The old token still accepted after rotation, the new token requiring a backend restart, rotation altering any file in the data directory other than api_token, or the rotate command's output containing the token value.
claims.text: Token rotation is atomic, takes effect without a backend restart or any data change, and immediately invalidates the old token: python -m glossa_lab.auth rotate replaces the file, the middleware's mtime-keyed re-read picks the new token up, and the command prints only the new fingerprint and the file path, never the value.

evidence.description: Spec 082 open-routes table (health rationale: supervision depends on an unauthenticated identity read; the payload is identity-only per Leg C C-08); test_api_token_auth.py asserts the health field set exactly and gates the three schema surfaces.

falsification_tests: The health payload containing any field beyond the identity set and the auth mode, the token or any credential material appearing in it, or /docs, /redoc, or /openapi.json answering 200 without the install token.
claims.text: GET /api/v1/health remains open and exposes only the served-identity fields (status, version, uptime_seconds, component, build) plus the auth mode word (auth: token or disabled) — no install data and no secret material — while /docs, /redoc, and /openapi.json require the token.

evidence.description: Spec 082 FR-006; test_api_token_auth.py covers dev-mode enforcement, missing-file self-generation (a protected route still 401s rather than opening), and the named-switch behavior including its health report.

falsification_tests: Any other configuration — dev mode, a missing token file, a missing environment, an installed-mode variant — under which a protected route answers without the install token; or GLOSSA_API_AUTH=off taking effect without the startup warning and the health payload's auth: disabled report.
claims.text: There is no silent open state: the only configuration under which protected routes answer without the install token is GLOSSA_API_AUTH=off, which logs a startup warning naming the switch and is reported by the health payload as auth: disabled.
